newsitem.title: RUSSIA: BA to expand ex-Soviet flights.
newsitem.headline: BA to expand ex-Soviet flights.

text.p: British Airways will begin regular flights between London and Riga, Latvia, setting up competition to private Russian carrier Transaero, a BA official said on Monday.
Geoff Rhodes, BA general manager Russia/CIS, said BA would start flights four times a week from March 30, operating Boeing 737 jets on the route.
Transaero's 737 planes fly five times a week between Moscow and London via Riga according to a code-sharing agreement with Riga International Airlines (RIA).
Rhodes said BA would also increase the frequency of its flights from London to the Ukrainian capital Kiev from three to five a week.
He also said BA would now fly Boeing 757s rather than Boeing 737s on its daily flights between London and Moscow and London and St Petersburg.

Rhodes said that BA's franchise, British Mediterranean, would begin regular flights from London to Tbilisi, Georgia, three times a week, operating a 124-seat A-320 jet from April 14, and from Tbilisi to the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek once every two weeks.
Currently BA flies from London to seven destinations in CIS states, making 34 flights a week.
Rhodes said that last year BA carried 116,988 passengers and 1,500 tonnes of cargo and mail on its London-Moscow route, and 101,461 passengers and 600 tonnes of cargo and mail from Moscow to London.
